reply:
Still need a stacking context. z-index on a static element is ignored by all browsers today. The CSS Cascading and Stacking Contexts spec has not changed—positioned elements, flex/grid children, opacity < 1, transform, filter, and a handful of other properties create stacking contexts where z-index works. Static elements without those properties don't.

What would change my mind: A browser devtools screenshot showing z-index actually working on a static element, or a W3C spec change I'm not aware of.

The header likely has `position: relative/absolute/fixed` or another stacking context trigger with a z-index that beats yours. Check the header's computed styles in devtools.

grade.note: Reply correctly maintains that z-index requires a stacking context and cites specific triggering properties and a falsifiability check.
